questions.question_english: The historic transition from a "vacancy-based" reservation roster to a "post-based" reservation roster in Indian public employment was mandated by which landmark Supreme Court judgment?
options_english: R.K. Sabharwal v. State of Punjab (1995)
M.R. Balaji v. State of Mysore (1963)

questions.explanation_english: In the landmark Constitution Bench ruling of R.K. Sabharwal v. State of Punjab (1995) 2 SCC 745, the Supreme Court held that the reservation roster must be operated on the basis of total posts in a cadre (post-based) rather than on recurring vacancies (vacancy-based). The Court ruled that once the prescribed percentage of posts allocated to a reserved category is achieved in a cadre, the roster becomes inoperative for that category, and subsequent appointments against vacancies arising from retirements/resignations of general category candidates cannot be usurped by reserved category candidates. To implement this binding constitutional principle, the DoPT issued OM No. 36012/2/96-Estt (Res) on 2nd July 1997, replacing vacancy-based rosters with post-based model rosters across all central establishments.
questions.explanation_hindi: सर्वोच्च न्यायालय की संविधान पीठ ने 'आर.के. सभरवाल बनाम पंजाब राज्य (1995) 2 SCC 745' के ऐतिहासिक मामले में यह व्यवस्था दी कि आरक्षण रोस्टर आवर्ती रिक्तियों (vacancy-based) के बजाय संवर्ग में कुल स्वीकृत पदों (post-based) के आधार पर संचालित होना चाहिए। न्यायालय ने स्पष्ट किया कि जब किसी संवर्ग में किसी आरक्षित वर्ग के लिए निर्धारित कोटा पूरा हो जाता है, तो रोस्टर उस वर्ग के लिए निष्प्रभावी हो जाता है। इसके पश्चात कार्मिक एवं प्रशिक्षण विभाग (DoPT) ने 2 जुलाई 1997 को ऐतिहासिक कार्यालय ज्ञापन जारी कर सभी केंद्रीय विभागों और संस्थानों में पद-आधारित रोस्टर प्रणाली अनिवार्य रूप से लागू की।

questions.explanation_english: Under Section 13(2) of the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013 (POSH Act), where the Internal Committee (ICC) or Local Committee (LCC) arrives at the conclusion that the allegation against the respondent has not been proved, it submits its inquiry report to the employer (or District Officer) recommending that no action is required to be taken in the matter. questions.explanation_english: Statement IV is INCORRECT. Under Rule 30 of the Income Tax Rules, 1962, tax deducted at source for any month from April to February must be deposited into the Central Government account on or before the 7th day of the immediately following month (for instance, October TDS must be remitted by 7th November). However, for tax deducted in the month of March (the fiscal year-end month), the statutory due date for deposit is extended up to 30th April (not 7th April) to accommodate annual reconciliation and financial year closing adjustments. Statements I, II, and III are all legally accurate deadlines: Q2 TDS return (Form 24Q) is due on 31st October, Form 16 must be issued by 15th June following the financial year, and October TDS is due on 7th November.

To establish foundational literacy as a precursor to Article 21A rights.
To enforce mandatory pre-schooling attendance across all state-run educational institutions.

questions.explanation_english: Modifying Article 45 via the 86th Amendment recognized early childhood care and education (ages 0-6) as essential for early cognitive development. key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) To establish foundational literacy as a precursor to Article 21A rights.

questions.question_english: The Central Educational Institutions (Reservation in Admission) Act, 2006, enacted to operationalize Article 15(5), provides for what percentage of reservation for Other Backward Classes (OBCs)?
questions.explanation_english: The Central Educational Institutions (Reservation in Admission) Act, 2006 (Act No. 5 of 2007) was enacted by Parliament pursuant to Article 15(5) to provide reservation in admissions to central educational institutions (including IITs, IIMs, Central Universities, and National Institutes). Section 3 of the Act mandates reservation of annual seats as follows: 15% for Scheduled Castes (SCs), 7.5% for Scheduled Tribes (STs), and 27% for Other Backward Classes (OBCs). The constitutional validity of this 27% reservation for OBCs in Central Educational Institutions was challenged and subsequently upheld by the Supreme Court in the landmark judgment Ashoka Kumar Thakur v. Union of India (2008), with the clarification that the 'creamy layer' must be excluded from availing this benefit.
questions.explanation_hindi: केंद्रीय शैक्षणिक संस्थान (प्रवेश में आरक्षण) अधिनियम, 2006 (2007 का अधिनियम संख्यांक 5) संसद द्वारा अनुच्छेद 15(5) के क्रियान्वयन हेतु बनाया गया था ताकि केंद्रीय शिक्षण संस्थानों (जैसे IITs, IIMs, केंद्रीय विश्वविद्यालयों आदि) में आरक्षण प्रदान किया जा सके। अधिनियम की धारा 3 के अनुसार कुल सीटों में से: 15% अनुसूचित जातियों (SC), 7.5% अनुसूचित जनजातियों (ST) और 27% अन्य पिछड़ा वर्ग (OBC) के उम्मीदवारों के लिए आरक्षित की गई हैं। केंद्रीय शैक्षणिक संस्थानों में इस 27% ओबीसी आरक्षण की संवैधानिक वैधता को सर्वोच्च न्यायालय ने 'अशोक कुमार ठाकुर बनाम भारत संघ (2008)' के ऐतिहासिक फैसले में वैध ठहराया था, जिसमें यह स्पष्ट किया गया था कि आरक्षण का लाभ देते समय 'क्रीमी लेयर' (मलाईदार परत) को अनिवार्य रूप से बाहर रखा जाना चाहिए।

questions.question_english: Section 35 of the POCSO Act, 2012 governs the procedure for recording evidence and completing trial. Within what period from taking cognizance of the offence must the child victim's evidence be recorded by the Special Court?

Within 30 days
Within 3 months

questions.explanation_english:
Section 35 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, 2012 sets strict timelines for legal proceedings to avoid revictimization of child victims:
1. Section 35(1) stipulates that the evidence of the child shall be recorded within a period of thirty days from the date of taking cognizance of the offence, and reasons for any delay must be recorded in writing by the Special Court.
2. Section 35(2) mandates that the Special Court shall complete the trial, as far as possible, within a period of one year from the date of taking cognizance of the offence.
The purpose of the 30-day requirement is to ensure prompt recording of fresh testimony while the child's memory is clear and before any external intimidation or secondary trauma can compromise the child's well-being or testimony.

2. धारा 35(2) के अनुसार, विशेष न्यायालय संज्ञान लेने की तिथि से एक वर्ष के भीतर विचारण (ट्रायल) को यथासंभव पूर्ण करेगा।
अतः धारा 35(1) के तहत बालक का साक्ष्य 30 दिनों के भीतर दर्ज किया जाना चाहिए। इसलिए विकल्प B सही उत्तर है।

questions.question_english:
Consider the following statements regarding the Standard Deduction available under Section 16(ia) for salaried taxpayers:
I. It is available uniformly as a flat deduction regardless of the actual expenses incurred by the employee.
II. It was reintroduced in lieu of the earlier tax exemptions for transport allowance and medical reimbursement.
III. Pensioners drawing pension taxable under the head 'Salaries' are also entitled to this deduction.
IV. The allowable deduction amount is prorated based on the number of months the employee worked in that financial year.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.question_hindi:
वेतनभोगी करदाताओं के लिए धारा 16(ia) के तहत उपलब्ध मानक कटौती (Standard Deduction) के संबंध में निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:
I. यह कर्मचारी द्वारा किए गए वास्तविक खर्चों की परवाह किए बिना एकमुश्त कटौती के रूप में समान रूप से उपलब्ध है।
II. इसे परिवहन भत्ता और चिकित्सा प्रतिपूर्ति पर मिलने वाली पूर्ववर्ती कर छूटों के स्थान पर पुनः लागू किया गया था।
III. 'वेतन' शीर्षक के तहत कर-योग्य पेंशन प्राप्त करने वाले पेंशनभोगी भी इस कटौती के पात्र हैं।
IV. अनुमत कटौती की राशि कर्मचारी द्वारा उस वित्तीय वर्ष में काम किए गए महीनों की संख्या के अनुपात में निर्धारित की जाती है।
उपर्युक्त कथनों में से कौन-से सही हैं?
options_english: I, II, and III only
II, III, and IV only
I and III only
I, II, III, and IV
options_hindi: केवल I, II और III
केवल II, III और IV
केवल I और III
I, II, III और IV
questions.explanation_english:
Statement I is correct: Standard deduction under Section 16(ia) is a statutory flat deduction available to all salaried taxpayers without requiring proof of any actual expenditure.
Statement II is correct: Finance Act 2018 reintroduced standard deduction to simplify tax compliance, replacing the earlier annual exemptions of ₹19,200 for transport allowance and ₹15,000 for medical reimbursement.
Statement III is correct: Pension received from a former employer is treated as salary under Section 17(1)(ii) of the Income Tax Act; hence, pensioners drawing such taxable pension are fully entitled to claim standard deduction up to ₹50,000.
Statement IV is incorrect: The standard deduction is an absolute statutory ceiling (₹50,000 or salary income, whichever is less) and is NOT prorated or calculated proportionally according to the number of months worked during the financial year. Even if an employee works for only a few months or days in the financial year, the full deduction up to their salary amount (subject to ₹50,000) is allowed.
Therefore, Statements I, II, and III only are correct.
questions.explanation_hindi:
कथन I सही है: धारा 16(ia) के तहत मानक कटौती एक वैधानिक एकमुश्त कटौती है जो कर्मचारी द्वारा किए गए किसी भी वास्तविक खर्च के प्रमाण के बिना सभी वेतनभोगियों को मिलती है।
कथन II सही है: वित्त अधिनियम 2018 द्वारा अनुपालन को सरल बनाने के लिए पूर्व में मिलने वाली ₹19,200 की परिवहन भत्ता छूट तथा ₹15,000 की चिकित्सा प्रतिपूर्ति छूट को समाप्त करके उसके स्थान पर मानक कटौती को पुनः लाया गया था।
कथन III सही है: पूर्व नियोक्ता से प्राप्त पेंशन को धारा 17(1)(ii) के तहत वेतन माना जाता है, इसलिए 'वेतन' शीर्षक में पेंशन दर्शाने वाले पेंशनभोगी भी ₹50,000 तक की मानक कटौती के पूर्ण पात्र हैं।
कथन IV गलत है: मानक कटौती की राशि वित्तीय वर्ष में काम किए गए महीनों के अनुपात (pro-rata) में निर्धारित नहीं होती। यदि किसी कर्मचारी ने वर्ष में कुछ महीने या दिन भी कार्य किया है, तब भी उसे उसके वेतन की सीमा तक पूरी ₹50,000 की कटौती की पात्रता होती है।
अतः केवल कथन I, II और III सही हैं।

questions.explanation_english:
Under Section 11(3) of the POSH Act, 2013, for the purpose of conducting an inquiry under Section 11(1), the Internal Complaints Committee (ICC) and the Local Committee (LC) are vested with the powers of a Civil Court under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (5 of 1908) when trying a suit in respect of:

(c) Any other matter which may be prescribed.

The ICC is an administrative quasi-judicial body and does not possess criminal jurisdiction. It has no authority to issue arrest warrants, sentence offenders to imprisonment, or freeze personal bank accounts. Its civil court powers exist strictly to enable complete evidentiary investigation and witness examination. Therefore, option (D) is correct.

questions.question_english: Under Section 31 of the POCSO Act, 2012, which procedural code governs the trial proceedings before a designated Special Court, save as otherwise expressly provided in the Act?

questions.explanation_english: Section 31 of the POCSO Act, 2012 provides that, save as otherwise provided in the Act, the provisions of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (CrPC) (including provisions regarding bail, bonds, and recording of evidence) shall apply to proceedings before a Special Court. For the purposes of these provisions, the Special Court is deemed to be a Court of Session, and the person conducting prosecution before it is deemed to be a Special Public Prosecutor (under Section 32). While the POCSO Act contains special child-friendly overrides—such as in-camera proceedings (Section 37), prohibiting direct, aggressive cross-examination of the child by the accused (Section 33(2)), and completing trials within one year (Section 35)—the foundational procedural framework remains the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.

Given below are two statements, one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R):
Assertion (A): Although Article 46 is a non-justiciable Directive Principle, constitutional courts have actively invoked it to sustain the constitutional validity of affirmative action programs under Part III.
Reason (R): Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles of State Policy are not mutually exclusive; rather, they are complementary and supplementary to each other in securing social and economic justice.

options_english: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true
questions.explanation_english:
Assertion (A) is true: While Directive Principles under Part IV are non-justiciable under Article 37, the Supreme Court has consistently held that they are not mere pious wishes. In cases such as State of Kerala v. N.M. Thomas (1976), Indra Sawhney v. Union of India (1992), and Ashoka Kumar Thakur v. Union of India (2008), the judiciary utilized Article 46 to interpret the scope of equality in Articles 15 and 16, affirming that substantive equality permits compensatory state measures.

Reason (R) is true: In the landmark Minerva Mills Ltd. v. Union of India (1980) decision, the Supreme Court held that the Indian Constitution is founded on the bedrock of the balance between Parts III and IV. To give absolute primacy to one over the other is to disturb the harmony of the Constitution. Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles are complementary and supplementary to each other.

Furthermore, Reason (R) correctly explains Assertion (A): It is precisely because Parts III and IV are complementary that courts can look to Article 46 to interpret and validate affirmative action measures under Part III without violating the constitutional scheme of equality.

questions.question_english: Which of the following statements INCORRECTLY compares the standard deduction available under 'Salaries' with the statutory deduction available under 'Family Pension'?
questions.question_hindi: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा कथन 'वेतन' (Salaries) के तहत मिलने वाली मानक कटौती और 'पारिवारिक पेंशन' (Family Pension) के तहत मिलने वाली वैधानिक कटौती की गलत तुलना करता है?
options_english: Standard deduction under the head 'Salaries' is a flat amount of up to ₹50,000.
Family Pension received by legal heirs is assessed under the head 'Income from Other Sources'.
The statutory deduction for Family Pension under Section 57(iia) is 33.33% of the pension or ₹15,000, whichever is less (under the old tax regime).
The standard deduction for Family Pension is ₹50,000, exactly identical to the deduction under regular salary.
options_hindi: 'वेतन' शीर्षक के तहत मानक कटौती ₹50,000 तक की एकमुश्त राशि है।
कानूनी वारिसों द्वारा प्राप्त पारिवारिक पेंशन का निर्धारण 'अन्य स्रोतों से आय' शीर्षक के तहत किया जाता है।
धारा 57(iia) के तहत पारिवारिक पेंशन के लिए वैधानिक कटौती पेंशन का 33.33% या ₹15,000 (जो भी कम हो) है (पुरानी व्यवस्था में)।
पारिवारिक पेंशन के लिए मानक कटौती ₹50,000 है, जो नियमित वेतन कटौती के बिल्कुल समान है।
questions.explanation_english:
Statement D is incorrect and hence the correct answer.
- Regular pension is received by the employee themselves from their former employer and is taxed under the head 'Salaries' (Section 17(1)). Salaried pensioners receive a flat standard deduction under Section 16(ia) of up to ₹50,000.
- In contrast, 'Family Pension' is received by the spouse or legal dependents after the death of the employee/pensioner. Since there is no employer-employee relationship between the recipient and the government/employer, family pension is taxable under the head 'Income from Other Sources' (Section 56).
- The deduction for family pension is governed by Section 57(iia), which restricts the deduction to 33.33% (one-third) of the family pension or ₹15,000, whichever is less (under the traditional provisions; enhanced to ₹25,000 under the New Regime by Finance Act 2024). It is definitely NOT ₹50,000 identical to regular salary.
questions.explanation_hindi:
कथन D गलत है और इसलिए यही सही उत्तर है।
- नियमित पेंशन सेवानिवृत्त कर्मचारी को स्वयं प्राप्त होती है और इसे आयकर अधिनियम की धारा 17(1) के तहत 'वेतन' (Salaries) माना जाता है, जिस पर धारा 16(ia) के तहत ₹50,000 तक की मानक कटौती मिलती है।
- इसके विपरीत, 'पारिवारिक पेंशन' कर्मचारी/पेंशनभोगी की मृत्यु के बाद उसके आश्रित परिजनों (पति/पत्नी आदि) को मिलती है। आश्रितों और नियोक्ता के बीच कोई सेवा-संबंध न होने के कारण पारिवारिक पेंशन पर 'अन्य स्रोतों से आय' (धारा 56) के तहत कर लगता है।
- धारा 57(iia) के अंतर्गत पारिवारिक पेंशन पर कटौती की सीमा पेंशन राशि का 33.33% (1/3 भाग) या ₹15,000 (जो भी कम हो) निर्धारित है। पारिवारिक पेंशन पर ₹50,000 की सामान्य वेतन मानक कटौती लागू नहीं होती।

questions.question_english: Which of the following correctly defines a "Composite Supply" under Section 2(30) of the CGST Act, 2017, which is particularly relevant when schools bundle educational and ancillary services?
options_english: A supply of two or more independent goods or services bundled together where all items are taxed at the highest applicable slab rate
A package of unrelated goods sold together at a single composite price in the open market
A supply involving exclusively non-taxable export goods and offshore digital educational content

A supply comprising two or more taxable supplies of goods or services which are naturally bundled and supplied in conjunction with each other in the ordinary course of business, one of which is a principal supply
questions.explanation_english: Under Section 2(30) of the CGST Act, 2017, a 'Composite Supply' means a supply made by a taxable person to a recipient consisting of two or more taxable supplies of goods or services or both, or any combination thereof, which are naturally bundled and supplied in conjunction with each other in the ordinary course of business, one of which is a principal supply. Under Section 8(a), the tax liability on a composite supply is determined entirely by the tax rate applicable to the principal supply. For instance, in a residential school providing education along with lodging and boarding, the principal supply is education; since schooling up to higher secondary level is exempt from GST under Entry 66 of Notification No. 12/2017-Central Tax (Rate), the entire composite package enjoys exemption. In contrast, artificially bundled supplies sold for a single price are 'Mixed Supplies' under Section 2(74) and taxed at the highest rate under Section 8(b).
questions.explanation_hindi: CGST अधिनियम, 2017 की धारा 2(30) के अनुसार, 'संयुक्त आपूर्ति' (Composite Supply) से तात्पर्य किसी करदाता द्वारा प्राप्तकर्ता को की गई वस्तुओं या सेवाओं की दो या दो से अधिक ऐसी आपूर्तियों से है जो सामान्य व्यावसायिक व्यवहार में स्वाभाविक रूप से एक साथ जुड़ी (naturally bundled) होती हैं, जिनमें से एक 'मुख्य आपूर्ति' (Principal Supply) होती है। धारा 8(a) के प्रावधानों के अनुसार, ऐसी संपूर्ण संयुक्त आपूर्ति पर मुख्य आपूर्ति की दर से ही कर लगाया जाता है। उदाहरण के लिए, किसी आवासीय (बोर्डिंग) स्कूल द्वारा विद्यार्थियों को शिक्षा के साथ-साथ छात्रावास और भोजन प्रदान करना एक स्वाभाविक रूप से बंडल संयुक्त आपूर्ति है, जिसमें मुख्य आपूर्ति 'शिक्षा' है। चूंकि विद्यालयी शिक्षा अधिसूचना सं. 12/2017 के तहत कर-मुक्त है, इसलिए पूरे पैकेज को छूट मिलती है। इसके विपरीत, अस्वाभाविक रूप से बंडल की गई आपूर्ति धारा 2(74) के तहत 'मिश्रित आपूर्ति' (Mixed Supply) कहलाती है और धारा 8(b) के तहत उन पर उच्चतम दर से कर लगता है।

questions.explanation_hindi: DoPT कार्यालय ज्ञापन संख्या 36039/1/2019-Estt (Res) के पैरा 4.2 में स्पष्ट रूप से प्रावधान है कि: "EWS स्थिति निर्धारित करने के लिए भूमि या संपत्ति धारण परीक्षण लागू करते समय विभिन्न स्थानों या विभिन्न शहरों/राज्यों में 'परिवार' द्वारा रखी गई संपत्ति को एक साथ जोड़ा (क्लब किया) जाएगा।" अतः यदि किसी परिवार के पास विभिन्न शहरों में 50-50 वर्ग गज के दो प्लॉट हैं या विभिन्न गांवों में कृषि भूमि के टुकड़े हैं, तो कुल क्षेत्रफल की गणना करने के लिए उन्हें संयोजित किया जाता है।

questions.explanation_english: Local journeys are strictly not reimbursable under LTC rules Local journeys, such as taxi or auto-rickshaw fares incurred while traveling from home to railway stations or for local sightseeing at the destination, are strictly non-reimbursable under Leave Travel Concession rules.
